newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia banks see first custody accounts in June.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia banks see first custody accounts in June.

text.p: Slovenian banks said on Wednesday they expected to open the first custody accounts for international portfolio investors in June.

Slovenia's biggest bank, state-owned Nova Ljubljanska Banka said it would charge a handling fee of 12 percent. Securities department head Tilka Kozelj said the bank expected to sign at least two contracts next month.
Probanka said it too expected to open its first custodian accounts next month and would charge 8.9 percent.
"We are preparing three custody account contracts," said Milana Lah, Probanka's global finance director.
Bank SKB said it was preparing custody account contracts but was unable to say when they would be signed.
Other banks gave no details on the matter.
The central bank blocked foreign portfolio investors in February when it ruled they had to open special accounts in order to trade in securities. Banks have been slow off the mark to meet the demand.

Analysts said share prices could rise by some 20 percent in the two to three months after the accounts are introduced but they were less bullish on long-term growth and warned that foreign investors would remain cautious.

"International investors believe the costs of the accounts are too high and they will remain on their guard in case the central bank introduces any other unexpected unpleasant decrees," one analyst said.

They estimated new foreign inflow of $17 million to the end of the year, compared with $30 million invested in the six weeks before the central bank ruling. -- Marja Novak, Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
